title: The notice-type to document-type mapping, the retention class and the write-once flag of each notice document type are not specified in any source read here
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7, RWB E1 052 Notice generation v1 v1 sections 4, 8 and 11; FSD P5 Document hub v3 AC-ALT-P5-003-01 and VR-P5-001-1 to VR-P5-001-3; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1 (DF-REF-218 to DF-REF-233 document_type); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-07 and R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria Background and AC2; 12.8 Contract fakes; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story generates a notice against a notice type (DEMAND, RECALL, GUARANTOR_NOTICE) and stores the PDF as a generated document, but no source read here states which document type of LOV-DOC-TYPE a notice type produces, nor the retention class and the write-once flag of the DEMAND_LETTER and GUARANTOR_NOTICE rows. The FSD gives the class and the flag of COURT_NOTICE (LEGAL10Y, write_once true) and of APPRAISAL_REPORT (GENERAL05Y, write_once false) only, in the fixture of another story. The story therefore takes the class and the flag from the document_type row in force and never types a value, the mapping is named as a data row, and the criteria assert the read rather than a value.
evidence: FSD P5 AC-ALT-P5-003-01 names the six types in version DOCTYPE-2026.11 and gives the class and flag of COURT_NOTICE and APPRAISAL_REPORT only; TSD P5 T3.1 defines retention_class and write_once on document_type but gives no row values; no source names a notice-type to document-type mapping
owner_role: Data steward and document type owner, with the Legal counsel and the P5 TechX squad
proposed: The document type load of RWB-P5-E1025-APP carries the DEMAND_LETTER and GUARANTOR_NOTICE rows with their class and flag, and the notice-type mapping row is added to the type or mapping table before the wave-1 test data is loaded

title: The rwb-document login, the request and answer field names of the generation path, the message text of MSG-P5-006, the container name, the index name, the Flyway step name and the P5 feature flag are not specified
source: TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1, T-A.2 API-P5-003, API-P5-004, API-P5-016 and API-P5-017; FSD P5 VR-P5-001-2 and AC-P5-001-01 (container path and MSG-P5-002 text); context pack P5 service facts and naming rules; Template and Rules v1 R4 and R9
section: 1 Story; 12.1; 12.7; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: The TSD names the request classes GenerateRequest and RegenerateRequest and the answer DocumentPage and Document by class only, and no source read here names their fields; the FSD names MSG-P5-006 without its text; the write-once legal container is named rwb-docs-legal for a court notice in one fixture only; and no source names the per-service login, the index, the migration step or a feature flag of this service. All of them are placeholders in the story, and the login is carried as the phrase 'the rwb-document login'.
evidence: TSD P5 T-A.2 gives GenerateRequest and RegenerateRequest by class name and states the regenerate carries a reason without naming the field; FSD P5 gives MSG-P5-006 as a code only; the ownership map names no index, migration file, flag or login
owner_role: Solution architect, with the P5 TechX squad
proposed: RWB-P5-E2026-CON names the request and reason fields of the two operations and the answer shape, RWB-PLT-DB fixes the login names, and the document type load publishes the container name and the message text of the document hub

title: This slice owns no legacy acceptance criterion while the Work Package lists all eleven legacy test cases for it
source: Work Package B2-P5-005 story line (acs empty, tcs_legacy of eleven IDs, secondary true); split plan entries RWB-P5-E1052-APP, RWB-P6-E1052-APP and RWB-ITG-E1052-ITG; RWB-P6-E1052-APP sections 7 and 19
section: 1 Story; 7 Acceptance criteria; 16 Test cases; 18 Traceability
description: The split gives RWB-P6-E1052-APP legacy AC1 to AC9 and the ITG slice the end-to-end proof of AC7, and gives this P5 slice none, while the Work Package hands the same eleven legacy test case IDs to every slice of the key. The story therefore writes nine new criteria under D-RCV-60 for the document side, lists the eleven legacy test cases with the part this service answers named in the Covers column, and states that the legacy criteria stay with P6. A reader or a traceability tool that expects every listed test case to cite a legacy criterion owned by the same story sees a mismatch.
evidence: The plan entry for RWB-P5-E1052-APP has an empty acs list and the same eleven tcs_legacy entries as the P6 stories; RWB-P6-E1052-APP section 19 records the split of the key
owner_role: Solution architect, with the traceability owner
proposed: The split plan records one owning story per legacy criterion and marks a secondary slice as test-case-bearing but criterion-free, so the traceability reports do not expect the two lists to match in every slice

title: The dependency rows of this slice name one contract only, while the pattern set names five platform contracts, the rwb-case reference-data contract and the generation contract of the service
source: Work Package B2-P5-005 story line (H, C, I, X); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-15 and DP-19; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T-A.2; RWB-P5-E2026-CON
description: The Work Package fixes the build row as empty and the contract row as one entry, RWB-P6-E1052-CON, while the pattern set names DP-03 (decision-record library), DP-07 (rwb-case reference-data contract and its client library), DP-09 (outbox library), DP-15 (Flyway sequence) and DP-19 (gateway-bff route). The operation's own request and answer shape is published by RWB-P5-E2026-CON, which is in no row either. The story therefore consumes those contracts against their fakes, names them in its preconditions and its pattern table, and records that no row carries them.
evidence: The Work Package rows carry one C entry and no H entry; the pattern table of R5.5 assigns a platform contract to each of DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-15 and DP-19; TSD P5 T-A.2 defines API-P5-016 with the request class GenerateRequest, whose contract is E2026's
owner_role: Solution architect, with the delivery lead
proposed: The plan adds the platform contract stories and RWB-P5-E2026-CON to the H or C rows of this slice, or records the service template's baseline contracts as implicit in every APP story

title: The monthly retention job JOB-17 is attributed to RWB-P5-E1052-APP by two service story files and to RWB-P5-E1017-APP and RWB-P5-E1041-APP by others, while this Work Package gives RWB-P5-E1052-APP the notice generation slice
source: Context pack P5 ownership rows (JOB-12, JOB-17); Architecture v5 slide 44 through the context pack; RWB-P5-E1055-APP section 12.6 and RWB-P5-E1065-APP section 12.6 (JOB-17 to RWB-P5-E1052-APP); RWB-P5-E1017-APP section 12.6 and RWB-P5-E1041-APP section 12.6 (JOB-17 to themselves); Work Package B2-P5-005
description: The service owns two jobs, JOB-12 document intake and JOB-17 retention. The retention Schedule and the retention_action rows are claimed by RWB-P5-E1017-APP and by RWB-P5-E1041-APP, and two other story files name RWB-P5-E1052-APP as the owner of JOB-17. This Work Package gives RWB-P5-E1052-APP the notice generation slice of legacy RWB-E1-052, which contains no job. The story therefore claims no Schedule, names the retention owner as RWB-P5-E1017-APP, and records the disagreement so the story map can settle it once.
evidence: RWB-P5-E1055-APP section 12.6 and RWB-P5-E1065-APP section 12.6 name RWB-P5-E1052-APP for JOB-17; RWB-P5-E1017-APP section 12.6 and RWB-P5-E1041-APP section 12.6 each name themselves; the legacy RWB-E1-052 story has no job at all
owner_role: Solution architect, with the delivery lead and the traceability owner
proposed: The story map records one owning story for JOB-17 (RWB-P5-E1017-APP), the other files are corrected at the next version, and RWB-P5-E1052-APP is recorded as the notice generation slice of the document hub with no Schedule
